owner.name: Wren Callahan
owner.bio: Wren Callahan started painting apartment turnovers on weekends during college and never really stopped. A lot of houses later, Bristlecone Paint Co. is a small, steady crew instead of a one-truck operation — but the rule from year one hasn't changed: real prep under every coat, or it doesn't go on the wall. Wren still walks every finished job with the homeowner before calling it done.

services.title: Deck & Fence Staining

faq.a: Two coats, minimum, on every job — three if the color shift needs it (deep reds and dark colors over white often do). That's built into the price, not an upcharge.
Yes. Patching nail holes, sanding rough spots, caulking gaps and taping edges happens before any paint opens. A repaint is only as good as what's underneath it.

faq.q: Do you offer low-odor or low-VOC paint?
faq.a: Yes — it's available at no extra charge on interior jobs. Ask for it if anyone in the house is sensitive to fumes or you just don't want to air the place out for two days.

faq.q: How long does a typical interior repaint take?
faq.a: A single room is usually a one-day job. A full-interior repaint runs two to four days depending on square footage and how much trim work is involved.

faq.q: Do I need to move my own furniture?
faq.a: No. We move what we can move safely and cover the rest — you don't need to empty a room before we show up.

faq.q: What if I don't love the color once it's on the wall?
faq.a: Bring a sample home and live with it for a day before we start — natural light changes everything. Once we've started a full room, a color change becomes a new job, so the visualizer and a sample chip up front save everyone a repaint.
